    - article:
      - heading "Precise Definitions" [level=3]
      - text: "Left-Hand Limit:"
      - paragraph: lim x→1⁻ f(x) = L means values approach L from x < 1.
      - text: "Right-Hand Limit:"
      - paragraph: lim x→1⁺ f(x) = L means values approach L from x > 1.
      - text: "Two-Sided Limit Exists:"
      - paragraph: Only when both one-sided limits exist and are equal.
    - article:
      - heading "⚠ Common Misconception" [level=3]
      - text: f(a) need not control the limit.
      - paragraph: The value at a point does not affect the limit. Limits depend on nearby values.
    - article:
      - heading "Worked Example" [level=3]
      - paragraph: lim x→1⁻ (x+1) = 2
      - paragraph: lim x→1⁺ (3−x) = 2
      - text: Both sides are equal, so the limit is 2.
